headline: BUET-led AI platform Tipsoi now used in 11 countries
summary: Developed by BUET engineers, the AI-powered workforce management platform is serving over 238,000 users across airports, banks, and healthcare facilities globally.
details: Tipsoi, an AI-driven workforce management platform created by a team of BUET engineers, is now operational in 11 countries, including Bangladesh, UAE, Mauritius, Malaysia, Turkey, and Pakistan.
The platform, developed by Innovess Technologies, serves over 1,200 organizations and 238,000 users through more than 10,000 active devices.
The technology is utilized across various sectors, including airports, banks, educational institutions, factories, healthcare facilities, and NGOs.
Innovess Technologies reported a nearly threefold growth in both domestic and international markets in 2025, leading to a recent update in their brand identity.
The company is now focusing on expanding its presence further into Europe and other Asian countries, marking a rare success for Bangladeshi software and hardware solutions in global markets.
The expansion is supported by investments from Accelerating Asia and Orbit Ventures, signaling a positive trend for the Bangladeshi startup ecosystem.
The company plans to roll out its new brand identity across its software platform, devices, website, and mobile applications over the coming months.
caption:
From BUET to the world! 🇧🇩

Bangladeshi AI platform Tipsoi is now powering workforce management in 11 different countries.

Tipsoi, an AI-driven workforce management platform created by a team of BUET engineers, is now operational in 11 countries, including Bangladesh, UAE, Mauritius, Malaysia, Turkey, and Pakistan.

The platform, developed by Innovess Technologies, serves over 1,200 organizations and 238,000 users through more than 10,000 active devices.

The technology is utilized across various sectors, including airports, banks, educational institutions, factories, healthcare facilities, and NGOs.

Innovess Technologies reported a nearly threefold growth in both domestic and international markets in 2025, leading to a recent update in their brand identity.

The company is now focusing on expanding its presence further into Europe and other Asian countries, marking a rare success for Bangladeshi software and hardware solutions in global markets.

The expansion is supported by investments from Accelerating Asia and Orbit Ventures, signaling a positive trend for the Bangladeshi startup ecosystem.

The company plans to roll out its new brand identity across its software platform, devices, website, and mobile applications over the coming months.

headline_marked: Bangladesh [[approves Starlink to export bandwidth]] to neighbouring countries
headline: Bangladesh approves Starlink to export bandwidth to neighbouring countries
summary: The government has permitted the satellite provider to carry unfiltered internet traffic from Bangladesh to other nations, potentially turning the country into a regional connectivity hub.
details: The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has approved a proposal allowing Starlink to export International Private Leased Circuit (IPLC) links to carry unfiltered internet traffic to neighbouring nations.
This marks the first time the government has formally permitted a satellite internet provider to engage in such an arrangement, aiming to position Bangladesh as a regional connectivity hub.

The state-owned Bangladesh Submarine Cable Company Limited (BSCCL) will be the primary supplier of the bandwidth, with Summit Communications Ltd and Fiber@Home Ltd as alternatives if BSCCL cannot meet capacity.

Unlike domestic bandwidth, which is filtered through government monitoring systems, the exported bandwidth will be unfiltered, as neighbouring countries like Nepal and Bhutan require high-quality, unrestricted connectivity.
The BTRC has strictly mandated that this unfiltered bandwidth must only serve foreign customers and cannot be used by anyone within Bangladesh, including foreign visitors.
To ensure compliance, Starlink must implement robust technical mechanisms to separate domestic and international traffic and provide real-time verification tools to the regulator.
Starlink officially began operations in Bangladesh on August 8, currently sourcing 80 Gbps of bandwidth for domestic use after receiving its license on April 29, 2025.
caption:
Bangladesh is set to become a regional internet hub. The government has officially allowed Starlink to export unfiltered bandwidth to neighbouring countries.

The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has approved a proposal allowing Starlink to export International Private Leased Circuit (IPLC) links to carry unfiltered internet traffic to neighbouring nations.

This marks the first time the government has formally permitted a satellite internet provider to engage in such an arrangement, aiming to position Bangladesh as a regional connectivity hub.

The state-owned Bangladesh Submarine Cable Company Limited (BSCCL) will be the primary supplier of the bandwidth, with Summit Communications Ltd and Fiber@Home Ltd as alternatives if BSCCL cannot meet capacity.

Unlike domestic bandwidth, which is filtered through government monitoring systems, the exported bandwidth will be unfiltered, as neighbouring countries like Nepal and Bhutan require high-quality, unrestricted connectivity.

The BTRC has strictly mandated that this unfiltered bandwidth must only serve foreign customers and cannot be used by anyone within Bangladesh, including foreign visitors.

To ensure compliance, Starlink must implement robust technical mechanisms to separate domestic and international traffic and provide real-time verification tools to the regulator.

Starlink officially began operations in Bangladesh on August 8, currently sourcing 80 Gbps of bandwidth for domestic use after receiving its license on April 29, 2025.
